title: Sentinel Lymph Node Mapping (ICG) in Endometrial, Cervical & Vulvar Cancers
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Uterine Neoplasms (2024)
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Cervical Cancer (2024)

steps.say: Near infrared fluorescence imaging with indocyanine green has replaced radiocolloids as the preferred modality for sentinel node mapping. Dual site cervical injections map both hemipelvises effectively.
steps.tx: **SLN mapping** utilizing near-infrared fluorescence with **Indocyanine Green (ICG)** (1 mg to **1.25** mg/mL) injected superficial (1 to 2 mm) and deep (1 cm) at **3 and 9 o'clock cervical injection** achieves excellent **bilateral mapping >85-90%** (**85** to **90** percent) in early endometrial and cervical carcinoma.

steps.say: The multi center FIRES trial provided prospective validation for sentinel node mapping in endometrial cancer. The technique demonstrated exceptionally high diagnostic accuracy.
steps.tx: The prospective multicenter **FIRES trial** (**Rossi 2017**) in endometrial cancer established an outstanding **NPV 99.6%** (negative predictive value **99.6** percent) and **sensitivity 97.2%** (**97.2** percent) for nodal metastasis, confirming that SLN biopsy safely **replaces lymphadenectomy** without compromising oncological outcomes in Stage **1** disease.

left.title: FIRES Trial Results (SLNB with ICG)
points: Sensitivity: 97.2% for identifying pelvic nodal metastasis
Lower extremity lymphedema reduced from 20% to under 2%

right.title: Systematic Full Lymphadenectomy
points: Removes 20 to 40 lymph nodes per patient
High incidence of chronic symptomatic lower-limb lymphedema
Higher rates of vascular injury, obturator nerve palsy, and lymphoceles

steps.say: Strict adherence to a standardized surgical algorithm is mandatory when sentinel lymph node mapping is employed. Any non mapping hemipelvis requires completion lymphadenectomy.
steps.tx: The **NCCN SLN algorithm** mandates: peritoneal inspection, excision of all fluorescent mapping sentinel nodes, **resection of suspicious nodes** regardless of fluorescence, and mandatory **hemipelvic lymphadenectomy for non-mapping** on any pelvic side where a sentinel node is not definitively identified, ensuring complete pathological staging and preventing unrecognized nodal metastasis.

nodes.label: Inject ICG at 3 and 9 o'clock cervix; retroperitoneal exploration
Excise all green-fluorescent sentinel lymph nodes
Palpate and resect any grossly enlarged or suspicious lymph node
Non-mapping hemipelvis: perform side-specific hemipelvic lymphadenectomy

steps.say: Pathological processing of sentinel lymph nodes requires ultrastaging with step sectioning and immunohistochemical stains. Cytokeratin antibodies detect minute occult tumor clusters.
steps.tx: Pathological evaluation requires a standardized **ultrastaging protocol**: gross longitudinal bisection along the long axis followed by **serial sectioning 50-250 um** (**50** to **250** um intervals) through the paraffin block and anticytokeratin immunohistochemistry using **cytokeratin AE1/AE3 IHC** (anti-cytokeratin AE**1**/AE**3** cocktail) to identify subtle metastatic deposits.

steps.say: International staging systems classify lymph node tumor volume into three distinct pathological categories. Prognosis correlates closely with metastatic tumor dimension.
steps.tx: Lymph node tumor volume is stratified into: **macrometastasis >2 mm** (**2.0 mm**), **micrometastasis >0.2 to <=2 mm** (greater than **0.2** mm to <=2 mm), and **isolated tumor cells (ITCs) <=0.2 mm** (clusters <=0.2 mm or under the **200 cell cutoff**).

rows: FIGO Stage IIIC / pN1 (indicates systemic chemotherapy + RT)
FIGO Stage IIIC / pN1(mi) (treated with adjuvant therapy)
FIGO Stage I / pN0(i+) (observation in low-risk disease)

steps.say: The therapeutic significance of isolated tumor cells in otherwise low risk endometrial cancer remains an area of active study. Low risk histology with isolated cells does not compromise outcome.
steps.tx: In early low-grade endometrioid endometrial carcinoma, the detection of **ITCs pN0(i+)** (staged as pN**0**(i+)) does not worsen **prognostic impact** (overall disease-free survival exceeds 95 percent), supporting safe **observation in low-risk** disease without adjuvant systemic chemotherapy or pelvic radiation when uterine risk factors remain strictly favorable.

left.title: Low-Risk Endometrial Cancer with ITCs (pN0(i+))
points: Stage IA Grade 1 or 2 endometrioid carcinoma
Excellent disease-free survival (>95%) without adjuvant systemic therapy
Observation alone or vaginal brachytherapy based on uterine risk features

right.title: High-Intermediate or High-Risk Histologies with ITCs
points: Grade 3 endometrioid, serous, or clear cell histology
Higher risk of distant systemic dissemination
Requires adjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy and external radiotherapy

steps.say: In early cervical cancer prospective trials confirmed that sentinel node mapping reduces post operative lymphedema. Bilateral detection is essential to ensure oncological safety.
steps.tx: In prospective cervical cancer trials (**SENTICOL I and II**), sentinel node mapping in Stage **1** and **2** tumors yielded significant **cervical cancer SLN** accuracy and **lymphedema reduction** (dropping morbidity by **30** percent), while establishing a strict **bilateral mapping requirement** before omitting pelvic dissection.

steps.say: Several clinical factors contribute to mapping failure during surgical procedures. Severe obesity and tumor blockage of lymphatic channels represent common impediments.
steps.tx: Recognized **mapping failure causes** include severe obesity with **BMI >40 kg/m2** (**40** kg/m2), previous retroperitoneal pelvic surgery, prior pelvic radiation, and extensive **tumor blockage of lymphatic channels**, producing an expected baseline **failure rate 10-15%** (**10** to **15** percent) requiring hemipelvic lymphadenectomy.
